prose_updates.tldr: A finite menu of prespecified donor stacks creates nonregular inference when validity is defined by an exact zero of a noisy baseline score. The panel procedures remain causal only under the explicit nonempty exact-close and shared-slope additive untreated-change conditions; zero score alone does not imply target coherence in the abstract Gaussian limit. The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. In the repaired bounded-spread score-only benchmark, \(b\) is observed exactly and only root-sample-scaled scores remain Gaussian: its exact honest expected-diameter value is zero for \(J=1\) and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), for arbitrary positive definite shared-control covariance and including multiple-close-donor faces. A data-free randomized hull attains the value; the covariance-aware deterministic score screen remains an honest operational comparator. The two-state subproblem retains the sharper separation-dependent value \(\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+\). Finite-sample transfer remains limited to bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs, and none of these conditional results validates the historical CMS comparison-state estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel, synthetic-control, and generic post-selection methods do not determine honest expected-diameter inference when validity is an exact zero-score face and several labels may be simultaneously valid. They also do not justify replacing a consistent unscaled effect estimate by exact observation in two-sided deficiency. The remaining transfer issue is distinct from the now-solved finite Gaussian decision problem.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused controls, and uncertainty about exact transport. A causal conclusion requires an exact population equality plus a model connecting the score to untreated changes. Ranked empirical balance supplies neither, and the abstract implication from zero scores to a common effect is an additional restriction rather than an algebraic fact.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact-close transport under the explicit shared-slope untreated-change model, gives uniformly honest simultaneous and pilot-adaptive procedures with fixed-separation oracle behavior, and proves that the full fixed-noise Gaussian frontier is infinite when effect spread is unrestricted. For the bounded-spread score-only repair it now derives the exact finite-face value \(0\) for \(J=1\) and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\), together with its attaining randomized kernel, arbitrary shared-control covariance, and multiple-zero faces. The two-face Mahalanobis formula remains the sharper separation-dependent restriction result, while the deterministic score screen is retained only as an honest comparator. Direct finite-sample transfer is proved only for bounded uniformly equicontinuous payoffs; unbounded-diameter and discontinuous-coverage transfer still require extra tail and boundary control.

prose_updates.related_work: The reviewed RTI material describes the CMS comparison-state workflow through ranked baseline distance, retained comparison states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting; it does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known population totals for every score component. Hence the workflow is a motivating and falsifiable use case, not evidence that the paper's exact-close assumptions held historically. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto obtain reference variation from many control groups, unlike the many-within-group, fixed-label regime here. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu study time-series synthetic-control inference rather than exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. motivate simultaneous protection; here the deterministic simultaneous score screen is kept as an operational comparator, whereas the exact bounded-spread finite-face minimax value is derived directly and attained by a data-free randomized rule. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey study argmax-winner selection; the present exact-zero-face model is not their argmax-selection model, and neither parameter class contains the other without changing both selection and estimand. Their work motivates only the separate pilot-adaptive oracle construction. Evans, Hansen, and Stark supply an acceptance-region expected-measure template, but their duality is not invoked because the needed domination, product measurability, and reduction from fixed sigma-finite expected measure to expected diameter are not established here. Andrews and Cheng, Andrews and Mikusheva, and Nussbaum motivate weak-limit and experiment-comparison questions but do not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction.
prose_updates.interpretation: The infinite full Gaussian frontier is an ill-posedness diagnosis, not a failure of simultaneous panel coverage: with unrestricted \(b\), nearly indistinguishable score faces can select effects separated by arbitrarily large amounts. Bounding the effect spread and observing \(b\) in the first-order score-only benchmark makes the problem finite. Its exact worst-case value is nevertheless positive for \(J\geq2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\): unique-zero faces can approach an excluded incoherent common-zero limit, forcing simultaneous inclusion of a grid of candidate effects. This least-favorable collision makes the exact constant independent of \(H\) and the positive definite covariance \(\Gamma\). The attaining randomized rule is a decision-theoretic benchmark; the deterministic covariance-aware score screen is often more operational but is not used to claim minimax attainment. The two-face formula still describes the sharper gain available at a fixed positive Mahalanobis separation. For the CMS workflow, exact calibration and untreated-trend transport must be prespecified and audited; good ranked balance cannot replace either condition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian benchmark has minimax expected diameter \(+\infty\). The repaired score-only bounded-spread experiment is solved exactly for every finite \(J\): the value is zero for one label and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\) under \(0<\alpha<1/2\). The result includes arbitrary positive definite shared-control covariance and multiple-zero faces, but its optimal kernel uses external randomization and exact observation of \(b\); the deterministic score screen is only an honest comparator. Evans--Hansen--Stark duality remains a template rather than a proof ingredient. For the panel-to-score-only step, the reduced statistic is uniformly close only in the weak topology under the stated assumptions. This suffices for bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs. Unbounded expected diameter additionally needs uniform integrability, discontinuous coverage needs boundary control, and two-sided Le Cam deficiency equivalence to exact observation of continuously varying \(b\) is false. The accepted pilot-adaptive construction and its oracle-equivalence statement are unchanged.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform causal coverage and fixed-separation oracle conclusions apply only to the triangular-array panel class satisfying consistency, stable group fractions, moment and covariance regularity, a nonempty exact close set, and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition. In the abstract Gaussian face problems, equality of the \(b_j\) values at simultaneous zero-score labels is separately imposed and is not implied by \(h_j=0\). The original unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. The exact finite frontier concerns the bounded-spread score-only experiment with exactly observed \(b\), \(H>0\), \(B>0\), positive definite \(\Gamma\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\): it is zero for \(J=1\) and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\), including multiple-close-donor faces. The Mahalanobis theorem separately gives the sharper exact value on any fixed two-face restriction. Finite-sample transfer is limited to bounded uniformly equicontinuous payoffs; unbounded-diameter transfer without uniform integrability, discontinuous-coverage transfer without boundary control, and two-sided deficiency equivalence to exact observation are not claimed. No reviewed source establishes the exact calibration assumptions for the historical CMS estimates.
